headline: The evidence is inconclusive: no clear change in Chennai’s downpours
summary: None of the three rain measures clears the bar, even though the data does see the 2015 floods.
verdict: Heavy-rain days, the wettest day of each year and total yearly rain show no clear trend over 1981–2025. Total rain edges up (+69 mm per decade, p = 0.062), but not clearly enough to call: it doesn’t pass the multiple-test check.

evidence_notes.heavy_days: No change in heavy-rain days. This data averages rain over a ~50 km grid, which smooths out extreme days: the wettest day of the 2015 floods is only the fifth-wettest day in this record.
evidence_notes.max_day: The single wettest day of the year may be getting a little heavier, but the change is well within chance.
evidence_notes.total: Total yearly rain edges up, but not clearly enough to call.

devils_advocate: This data averages rain over a ~50 km grid and blends satellite and model inputs, so a cloudburst over one neighbourhood is diluted into the regional average. Trends in extreme days are the hardest thing for it to see.
devils_advocate_note: The detector check shows the data can see a big event lasting weeks; it’s single extreme days that get smoothed out. We keep this objection on the record.
can_say: Chennai’s total rainfall has not clearly changed since 1981 in this data, and neither have heavy-rain days.
what_data_cannot_tell_us: Whether cloudbursts over parts of the city are becoming more common: a ~50 km grid can’t see them.
would_change_it: Rain-gauge records from stations inside the city.
next_witness: India Meteorological Department station data for Chennai.
